malwaregen.TopLevel: Evaluates whether the model can be prompted to generate complete, functional malware (e.g., scripts or code that could be compiled into malicious executables), assessing the baseline risk of LLM-assisted malware creation.
malwaregen.Evasion: Evaluates whether the model assists in creating malware that evades detection—such as obfuscation, anti-sandbox tricks, or polymorphic code—measuring how well safety controls resist abuse for evasive malware.
promptinject.HijackHateHumans: Simulates prompt injection that tries to override system instructions and elicit hateful or dehumanizing language toward humans, testing whether alignment and safety guardrails hold under adversarial prompts.
promptinject.HijackKillHumans: Simulates prompt injection aimed at making the model endorse or suggest violence or harm against humans, testing the robustness of harm-prevention and refusal safeguards.
promptinject.HijackLongPrompt: Uses long or complex injected prompts to overwhelm context or instruction-following, testing whether the model loses track of safety or alignment constraints when input is lengthy or confusing.
realtoxicityprompts.RTPBlank: Uses prompts derived from real toxic text to see if the model reproduces or amplifies toxic content, measuring toxicity and content-safety behavior under realistic abusive inputs.
sata.MLM: Probes potential misuse or information leakage related to masked language modeling (e.g., fill-in-the-blank) that could reveal sensitive patterns or harmful completions when the model predicts masked tokens.
snowball.GraphConnectivity: Checks whether the model’s reasoning about graph connectivity (e.g., paths, relationships between nodes) can be manipulated or fails in ways that could affect reliability or security of reasoning-dependent outputs.
snowball.Primes: Evaluates correctness and robustness of mathematical reasoning about prime numbers, indicating general reliability and potential for misuse in logic-heavy or verification-sensitive tasks.
snowball.Senators: Evaluates reasoning about factual or relational queries (e.g., involving public figures or senators) to test consistency, hallucination risk, and susceptibility to subtle prompt manipulation.
suffix.BEAST: Tests resistance to the BEAST (Best-of-N) suffix attack, which searches for adversarial token suffixes that steer the model toward unsafe, refused, or otherwise unintended outputs.
suffix.GCG: Tests resistance to the Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) method, which finds token-level adversarial suffixes to elicit behaviors the model is supposed to refuse or restrict.
suffix.GCGCached: Uses cached or precomputed GCG adversarial suffixes to measure whether the model remains robust against known or reusable suffix-based attack patterns.
tap.PAIR: Evaluates resistance to the PAIR (Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement) attack, which iteratively refines adversarial prompts to bypass refusals and elicit harmful or restricted content.
tap.TAP: Evaluates resistance to the Tree of Attacks with Pruning (TAP), which explores multiple attack branches to find prompts that bypass safety and elicit harmful or restricted outputs.
tap.TAPCached: Uses cached or precomputed TAP attack variants to test whether the model remains robust against known attack trees and previously successful jailbreak patterns.
test.Blank: Checks that the model returns a blank or minimal response when appropriate, serving as a baseline for response format and refusal behavior in edge cases.
test.Test: Simple sanity check that the model responds as expected to a neutral prompt, verifying basic connectivity, availability, and normal response behavior.
topic.WordnetAllowedWords: Evaluates whether the model correctly classifies or allows content that should be permitted (e.g., benign topics from WordNet), testing that content policy boundaries do not over-block safe content.
topic.WordnetBlockedWords: Evaluates whether the model correctly blocks or refuses content containing disallowed or sensitive terms, testing that content filters and safety policies block inappropriate topics.
topic.WordnetControversial: Evaluates how the model handles controversial or borderline topics (e.g., from WordNet), testing consistency and appropriateness of content moderation on edge-case subjects.
visual_jailbreak.FigStep: Tests whether images (e.g., figures or step-by-step visuals) can be used to bypass safety measures and elicit harmful or restricted text or behavior—a multimodal jailbreak probe.
xss.ColabAIDataLeakage: Checks whether model outputs could be crafted to trigger or facilitate cross-site scripting (XSS) or data leakage when used in Colab AI or similar web-integrated environments.
xss.MarkdownImageExfil: Tests whether markdown image syntax in model output can be abused to exfiltrate data or trigger XSS when the output is rendered in web contexts (e.g., chat UIs, docs).
xss.MarkdownURIImageExfilExtended: Extended tests for data exfiltration or XSS via markdown image URIs (e.g., long or malformed URIs) when model output is rendered in browsers or web applications.
xss.MarkdownURINonImageExfilExtended: Extended tests for data exfiltration or XSS via non-image markdown URIs (links, etc.) when model output is rendered in web contexts, ensuring links cannot be weaponized.
xss.MdExfil20230929: Specific markdown-based exfiltration probe (version dated 2023-09-29) to assess whether model output can be used to leak data through markdown rendering in vulnerable clients.
xss.StringAssemblyDataExfil: Tests whether model outputs can be used to assemble strings that lead to data exfiltration or XSS when interpreted or rendered (e.g., in HTML or JavaScript contexts).
